cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the parsed schema from simple-schema.json (no exception)
cases.description: Pass a valid classpath URI pointing to a well‑formed JSON schema file. The method should delegate to the overload, load the schema and return a non‑null JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the parsed schema from the file (no exception)
cases.description: Pass a valid file‑system URI that points to a readable JSON schema file. The method should correctly convert the URI to a SchemaLocation and return the loaded JsonSchema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (or a SchemaLoadingException wrapped in a RuntimeException if network is unavailable)
cases.description: Pass a remote HTTP URI. The factory should attempt to load the schema via the default SchemaLoader. The test verifies that the call path is exercised without throwing an unexpected exception.

cases.expected: SchemaLoadingException (or a RuntimeException) indicating that the resource cannot be found
cases.description: Provide a well‑formed URI that points to a resource that does not exist. The method should still delegate to the overload, which will fail to locate the schema and raise an appropriate exception.

cases.expected: SchemaLoadingException (or a RuntimeException) indicating file not found
cases.description: Pass a file URI that points to a non‑existent file. The factory should attempt to read the file and propagate the loading failure.

group: Edge cases – Null and malformed URIs

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: Calling getSchema(null) should immediately throw a NullPointerException because the method dereferences schemaUri to call toString().

cases.expected: URISyntaxException wrapped in IllegalArgumentException or RuntimeException
cases.description: Supply a syntactically malformed URI. The factory will attempt to create a SchemaLocation from the string; the underlying implementation should raise an exception that the test can assert.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance created with the default SchemaValidatorsConfig (verify that config properties such as 'typeLoose' are false)
cases.description: Even though getSchema(URI) does not expose the config, it must use the factory's createSchemaValidatorsConfig(). The test inspects the returned JsonSchema's validation configuration to ensure the default config is applied.

group: URI with YAML extension – classpath resource

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance parsed from the YAML file (no exception)
cases.description: Pass a valid classpath URI that points to a well‑formed YAML schema. The factory should detect the .yaml extension, use the YAML mapper, and return a non‑null JsonSchema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the parsed schema (no exception)
cases.description: Supply a classpath URI that contains percent‑encoded characters (space). The method must correctly decode the path and load the schema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance identical to the one loaded from the same URI without fragment (no exception)
cases.description: A fragment part after ‘#’ should be ignored when locating the schema. The returned JsonSchema must be the same as when the fragment is omitted.

cases.expected: Two successive calls to getSchema(uri) return the same JsonSchema instance (reference equality)
cases.description: Invoke getSchema(uri) twice in the same factory instance and verify that the second call returns the cached JsonSchema rather than creating a new object.

cases.expected: RuntimeException (or SchemaLoadingException) indicating that the scheme is not supported
cases.description: Provide a URI with a scheme that the default SchemaLoader does not understand. The method should propagate a clear exception rather than silently succeed.

cases.expected: SchemaLoadingException (or RuntimeException) because the location resolves to a directory, not a file
cases.description: Pass a URI that resolves to a directory. The loader should reject it and throw an appropriate exception.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance parsed from the file (no exception)
cases.description: Test that the factory treats scheme case‑insensitively; a FILE scheme in upper case must be handled like a normal file URI.

cases.expected: JsonProcessingException (or SchemaLoadingException wrapping it) indicating JSON parsing failure
cases.description: The URI points to a classpath resource that contains syntactically invalid JSON. The factory should attempt to read the content, fail during parsing, and propagate a parsing‑related exception.

cases.expected: JsonProcessingException (or SchemaLoadingException wrapping it) indicating YAML parsing failure
cases.description: The URI points to a YAML schema file with incorrect indentation / syntax. The factory must detect the .yaml extension, use the YAML mapper, and surface the parsing error.

group: Schema with invalid $ref – referenced schema not found

cases.expected: SchemaLoadingException (or RuntimeException) reporting that the $ref target cannot be resolved
cases.description: The provided schema contains a $ref that points to a non‑existent schema file. During loading the factory should attempt to resolve the reference and throw an exception when the target cannot be located.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or SchemaLoadingException) indicating that the meta‑schema IRI is not recognized
cases.description: The schema declares an "$schema" attribute whose IRI does not correspond to any known JsonMetaSchema. The factory should fail while trying to load the meta‑schema.

cases.expected: IOException (or SchemaLoadingException wrapping it) caused by access‑permission failure
cases.description: The file exists but the process lacks read permissions. When the factory attempts to open the InputStream, an IOException should be thrown and propagated.

group: Circular reference detection – recursion limit exceeded

cases.expected: StackOverflowError or SchemaLoadingException indicating circular reference / recursion depth exceeded
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref chain that eventually references itself, creating a circular dependency. The factory must detect the recursion limit and raise an appropriate exception rather than entering an infinite loop.
